summary: Completed the first scenario-complete Space Exploration Technologies listed-equity review using current SEC primary evidence and the canonical 2026-08-04 volume anomaly. Q2 revenue grew 91.9% to USD 7.814 billion and Connectivity produced USD 1.656 billion of segment operating income, but Space and AI remained loss-making, first-half property and equipment purchases reached USD 28.476 billion, customer concentration and controller governance are material, and the USD 125.33 mark embeds extreme revenue multiples. The deterministic assessment recorded Hold, Watch, 72 quality, low confidence, and USD 50/USD 110/USD 195 bear/base/bull fair values with USD 109 probability-weighted value. Allocation remains ineligible; no strategy, signal, paper order, issue, or follow-up operation was created.

evidence.claim: The Q2 SEC filing reported USD 7.814 billion revenue, USD 143 million operating loss, USD 541 million net loss, USD 3.538 billion adjusted EBITDA, 12.0 million Starlink service lines, USD 66 subscriber ARPU, USD 100.009 billion cash plus marketable securities, USD 39.364 billion debt and finance leases, USD 3.466 billion first-half operating cash flow, USD 28.476 billion first-half property and equipment purchases, and USD 47.461 billion backlog.

The SEC Form 8-K establishes that Space Exploration Technologies issued its second-quarter 2026 earnings release on August 4, the same date as the canonical volume-anomaly session; numerical conclusions use the filed quarterly report.

The final SEC prospectus priced 555,555,555 Class A shares at USD 135, expected approximately USD 74.4 billion of net proceeds, documented option and RSU overhang and common-control transaction history, and left Elon Musk with approximately 82.4% of voting power immediately after the offering.

The canonical alert measured a 16.15% adjusted-close decline from 2026-07-07 through 2026-08-04, followed by a 9.43% one-session rise to USD 125.33 on 140.6 million shares and a 3.4588 volume-anomaly factor. RSI was neutral at 46.96 and the 36-observation history was insufficient for 50-day and 200-day averages. The review classified this as material mixed post-earnings repricing and timing risk, not noise or a paper-buy signal.

Deterministic assessment version 2 derived USD 109 probability-weighted fair value, -13.0296% expected return, -6.5148% confidence-adjusted expected return, USD 88 buy-below price, -13.9364% margin of safety, Hold canonical rating, Watch portfolio action, Watch conviction tier, 72 quality, and allocation ineligibility with complete threshold-frontier reasons.
